vulnerable.evidence: Malicious braceExpand pattern (n=50000) took 1811ms (>= 1500ms threshold), indicating ReDoS/catastrophic backtracking. maliciousThrew=false

fixed.evidence: Malicious braceExpand pattern (n=50000) completed in 0ms (below threshold), no DoS observed. maliciousThrew=false; resultType=array[1]

oracle.explanation: The oracle first proves minimatch's public API works correctly on a benign brace-expansion pattern and a simple match. It then feeds minimatch.braceExpand a pathological deeply-nested unbalanced-brace pattern ('{' repeated 50001 times) which is known to trigger catastrophic backtracking in the pre-3.0.5 brace-expansion/nobrace-shortcut regex used by minimatch 3.0.4. Elapsed wall-clock time is measured without relying on an interrupting timer; if it exceeds a 1.5s bounded threshold the exploit is flagged as succeeded (ReDoS), otherwise it's reported blocked. In the patched version (>=3.0.5), the tightened non-greedy nobrace regex and the new assertValidPattern length guard make this call resolve near-instantly, so exploit_succeeded will be false while operation_completed remains true since setup and benign checks already passed. Any failure during setup or the benign check keeps operation_completed false.

attempts.explanation: The oracle first proves minimatch's public API works correctly on a benign brace pattern (braceExpand and minimatch matching a simple '{b,c}' alternation), setting operation_completed=true only after that succeeds. It then feeds minimatch.braceExpand a crafted pathological pattern (many nested braces combined with trailing negation markers) designed to trigger catastrophic backtracking in the pre-3.0.5 regex-based brace-detection shortcut (`pattern.match(/\{.*\}/)`) and related parsing logic. Execution time is measured with Date.now() around the call; if the malicious call takes at least 2000ms (a bounded but clearly distinguishing threshold reachable by the vulnerable version within a few seconds, while the patched version's length/shape validation and non-greedy brace-detection regex resolve it almost instantly), exploit_succeeded is set true. No timers, process spawning, or filesystem/network access are used; only the minimatch package itself is exercised. Any exception during setup or the benign call is caught and reported with operation_completed=false, never misreported as exploit_succeeded=false due to a crash.
attempts.validation_reason: Expected vulnerable=EXPLOIT_SUCCEEDED and fixed=EXPLOIT_BLOCKED; got vulnerable=EXPLOIT_BLOCKED and fixed=EXPLOIT_BLOCKED.
